saved_data.content/data/courses/text-classification:
id: course/text-classification-from-scratch
purpose: Teach end-to-end text classification through an AI-written-text
  detection case study and the history of text-classification architectures,
  then apply the ideas in a multi-task Jev-like decision model implemented with
  a pretrained ModernBERT encoder.
audience: Python practitioners who know basic supervised learning and want to
  build, evaluate, and serve text classifiers; GPU training and external APIs
  are optional extensions.
planned:
  summary: Define the task and label contract; audit provenance; construct
    grouped splits; establish a TF-IDF baseline; trace the history from
    bag-of-words through neural and transformer classifiers; compare
    task-specific models, prompted LLMs, and structured general-purpose decision
    APIs; evaluate calibration, errors, task transfer, efficiency, and
    deployment; and finish by implementing and evaluating a Jev-like
    Choice/Noul/Score model with a shared ModernBERT candidate-scoring head.
actualized:
  summary: Authored the course home, system overview, and ten chapters.
    Augmented the model-family, evaluation, efficiency, deployment, and capstone
    chapters with classifier history, structured decision APIs, calibration, and
    cross-task generalization. The capstone now specifies a multi-task
    ModernBERT implementation of a Jev-like decision interface, including
    held-out task transfer and probability calibration. Added exercises and
    rendered the affected notebooks to HTML for syntax checks.
